The present appeal was preferred by the appellants on 18.07.2016 and was assigned to the then learned FSSA Court and after administrative directions vide order no. 12072-12106/ Judl.
/NDD/PHC/ND dated 01.10.2019 it was assigned to this court for disposal of the same as per law.

By way of present appeal, the appellants Munish Kumar and Ram Gopal herein has challenged the judgment dated 30.04.2016 and order on the point of sentence dated 11.05.2016 passed by the then learned ACMM-II, PHC, New Delhi vide which the appellants/accused persons were held guilty for commission of offences punishable under sections2(ia)(a)&(m) of PFA Act r/w 44A, PFA Rules &
Section 16(1)(a) r/w Section 7 of PFA Act, 1954, both the appellants were awarded sentence to undergo Simple Imprisonment for 01 year (each) with fine of Rs. 20,000/- (each) for commission of aforesaid offences and in dafault of payment of fine to undergo Simple Imprisonment of one month.

The complaint was then filed in the court on 20.07.2006 alleging violation of Section 2(ia)(j) and (m) of PFA Act read with Rules, 28,29 and 30 of PFA Rules, as punishable under Section 7/16(1A) of PFA. Act.

The appellant was summoned by the learned trial court vide order dated 20.07.2006 for 18.04.20076.

After filing their appearance, the appellants moved an application under section CA no. 8687/2016 Munish Kumar Ram Gopal Vs. Delhi Admn (PFA) Pages 3 of 14 13(2) of the PFA Act thereby exercising their right to get the second counterpart of the sample analyzed from the Central Food Laboratory (CFL).

sentences.text: The application was allowed and a counterpart was sent for analysis to CFL.
After examination, Director gave certificate dated 04.09.2006 opining the sample to be in violation of Rule 44A of PFA Rules, having tested positive for Kesari Dal flour.
Synthetic colour tartrazine was also detected but there was no observation that it was beyond the permissible limits.
5. Thereafter matter was listed for pre-charge evidence, wherein the complainant examined PW-1 Ms. Sonika Singh and PW-2 Sh C.B.Boora, Food Inspector.

On the basis of testimony of these witnesses, initially on 25.09.2009 charge was framed against the appellants/accused persons and thereafter amended charge was framed against them on 28.08.2012 for commission of offences punishable u/s 7/16(1A) PFA Act for violation of Section 2(ia)(a)(j) and (m) of PFA Act and Rule 44 of PFA Rules, alleging therein that on 29.11.2005 at about 04.45 p.m, appellant no. 1 being the Vendor of "M/s Deepak Sweets & Restaurant" Shop no.
122, Mehar Chand Market, Lodhi Colony,New Delhi 110003 sold approximately 1500 grams of 'Boondi Ke Ladoo' taken from an open tray lying there, having no label declaration, meant for human consumption to Sh. C.B.Boora, Food Inspector in presence of LHA and witnesses for analysis and accordingly it was analyzed by the Director vide his report dated 04.09.2006 vide which he found sample was not conforming to the standards i.e. in contravention of Rule 44A of PFA Rules, 1955 as CA no. 8687/2016 Munish Kumar Ram Gopal Vs. Delhi Admn (PFA) Pages 4 of 14 test for Kesari Dal flour was found positive to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

sentences.text: 6.1 During trial after the examination and detailed cross examination of three witnesses of the department prosecution evidence was closed and matter was fixed for Statement of accused.

7. The statement of appellant/accused persons were recorded under section 313 Cr.PC separately in which they pleaded their innocence and appellant no.1 Munish Kumar stated that sample of Boondi Ke Ladoo was lifted on the above mentioned date, however, it was not lifted in his presence as he was not present there ; no payment was made to him by the food Inspector ; sample proceeding was not conducted in his presence; PA report is wrong ; consent was granted without application of mind.
He further stated that the PA report and CFL report were different and sample failed due to bad sampling and due to delay in the analysis of the sample commodity i.e. Boondi Ke Ladoo.
They both preferred to lead defence evidence but did not produce any witness in their defence and defence evidence was closed vide order dated 07.02.2013.

7.1 After hearing the arguments of both the parties, both the appellants/accused persons were convicted by the learned trial court CA no. 8687/2016 Munish Kumar Ram Gopal Vs. Delhi Admn (PFA) Pages 5 of 14 for commission of offence punishable under section punishable u/s 7/16(1)(a)
PFA Act for violation of Section 2(ia)(a) and (m) of PFA Act, 1954.

entities.text: Munish Kumar Ram Gopal Vs. Delhi Admn (PFA)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. The learned trial court in its impugned judgment dated 30.04.2016 observed that the samples had been collected according to the prescribed procedures from the premises of vendor ; the case in hand would therefore covered under Section `(1a)(a) of PFA Act as there is sufficient evidence to show that it was not of the nature, substance or quality which it is ''purported' to be as per PFA Rules ; the case would fall under Section 2(ia)(m) of PFA Act as the constituent of Kesari dal flour is present in quantities not within the prescribed limits, being totally prohibited.
However, no offence under section 2(1a)(j) was made out in view of the CFL report that did not specify that the quantity of synthetic colour present was in excess of the prescribed limits.

Use of Munish Kumar vs Delhi Administration/ on 18 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124526483/
3

such synthetic colour is permitted in sweets and unless they are detected in quantities beyond permissible limits, no violation of Section 2(ia)(j) would be there ; violation of Section 2(ia)(a) and (m) is punishable under Section 16(i)(a) of PFA Act and appellants committed the offence punishable u/s 7/16(1)(a) PFA Act.

The appellants were accordingly convicted and sentenced by the learned trial court and aggrieved by the said judgment and order on quantum of sentence dated 11.05.2016, the present appeal has been preferred by the appellant.
9.(I) The appellant has assailed the judgment and order on sentence passed by the learned trial court by urging various CA no. 8687/2016 Munish Kumar Ram Gopal Vs. Delhi Admn (PFA) Pages 6 of 14 grounds.
II) Alternatively, on the quantum of sentence, relying upon the new legislation, it was pleaded that the case of the appellants be considered sympathetically in the light of the preposition of law laid down by the Hon'ble Courts pursuant to coming of new legislation that is Food Safety & Standards Act.
10.

sentences.text: During the course of argument on 14.01.2021, learned counsel for the appellants submitted that appellants are not challenging the merits of the case/ conviction decided by the learned trial court vide judgment dated 30.04.2016 and is confining their appeal limited to the quantum of sentence only awarded to them vide order dated 11.05.2016 ; and to affirm their submissions, appellants have tender their affidavit duly sworn and notarized by the Oath Commissioner, in this regard and prayed that a lenient view be taken against them by giving the benefit of New Legislation as FSSAI.

11. Learned counsel for the Delhi Admn./Food Department, objected to the same and submitted that according to submission of appellant, prosecution has established its case and he be sentenced with strict punishment in terms of old Act wherein minimum punishment is prescribed and no leniency should be shown to the convict as it is a serious offence of food adulteration article / commodity leading to hazardous consequences on the health or body of a person.
12.

I have carefully gone through the available record as well as trial court record, have heard the submissions of learned counsel for both the parties at length and have also gone through the CA no.
8687/2016 Munish Kumar Ram Gopal Vs. Delhi Admn (PFA) Pages 7 of 14 judgments relied upon by the parties.

entities.text: Munish Kumar Ram Gopal Vs. Delhi Admn (PFA)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. In light of above submissions and discussion particularly when the affidavit of appellants to this effect was filed on record, I find no valid and legal reasons to interfere with the well reasoned judgment of the learned trial court.
The findings of the learned trial court with respect to the conviction of the appellant for the offence punishable under 16(1)(a) of the PFA Act read with Section 7 of the PFA Act, 1954 are upheld.
II. Now Coming to the alternate plea of giving benefit of new legislation to the appellant/ accused.

Munish Kumar vs Delhi Administration/ on 18 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124526483/
4 14.
It is argued by learned counsel for the appellant that on the date of pronouncement of judgment/order on sentence, the PFA Act, 1954 was repealed and new act has thereafter come into operation.

It is stated that the court should give benefit of the new legislation to the accused vide which the punishment provided under the old act has been diluted to a considerable extent, and that the offence for which the accused/appellant has been convicted now falls under the category of "Unsafe Food" punishable under section 59(1) of the new Act i.e Food and Safety Standards Act,
2006 (hereinafter called FSSAI) punishable upto six months and fine of upto Rs. One lac only.
15.

It was argued by learned counsel for the appellant that appellant no.1 is a man of young age,however, appellant no. 2 is aged about 72 years, both are the respectable person of society, have deep roots in the society, have responsibility towards their family, not keeping good health, not involved in any other case, and CA no. 8687/2016 Munish Kumar Ram Gopal Vs. Delhi Admn (PFA)
Pages 8 of 14 have left the said business and for their livelihood dependent upon farming and prayed that a lenient view be taken against them in the light of the provisions of law under the new Act.

sentences.text: 15.1 Further it is stated that case pertains to the year 2005, the appellant/accused persons have faced the trial almost 15 years which by itself is a sufficient punishment and the hardships faced by them has caused great mental agony, stress and rigors of trial during the said period.

It is also stated that now a days special circumstances exists due to outbreak of pandemic of Covid-19 and there are chances of appellants being infected with virus in case imprisonment of sentence is awarded to them.

15.2 In support of his submissions qua the consideration of the case under new legislation, learned counsel for appellant had relied upon the judgment of Nemi Chand Vs. State of Rajasthan ( Crl. Appeals No.
214 and 215 of 2016, vide order dated 10.03.2016, as corrected vide order dated 17.03.2016, as reported in 2016 (1) FAC 203 ) of Hon'ble Supreme Court and earlier judgment T Barai Vs. Henry 1983 ( ) SCC 177.
15.3

sentences.text: Per contra, learned SPP, strongly opposed the submissions advanced by learned counsel by addressing that the sentencing cannot be done in new Act since the definition of many offences are changed in the new Act including this particular offence of which accused is charged.
Definition of major offences like "adulteration" and "misbranding" have been changed.
Now FSSAI have definition "substandard food", "food containing extraneous matter" "unsafe food" and misbranded food".

Due to this reason, the ingredients have CA no. 8687/2016 Munish Kumar Ram Gopal Vs.
Delhi Admn (PFA) Pages 9 of 14 changed and thus there is no way in which the old offences could be related to new offences.

sentences.text: 15.4 In the present case, the offence was that the food article i.e. Boondi KeLadoo was found adulterated and was unfit for human consumption having tested positive for Kesari Dal flour.
Synthetic colour tartrazine was also detected but there was no observation that it was beyond the permissible limits .

This was violation of Rules under PFA Rules and thus termed as adulteration in view of Section 2(1a)(a) (m) of the PFA Act and thus consequently punishable under section 16(1)(a)
of PFA Act read with Section 7 of PFA Act.
15.5
That now in the FSSAI such adulteration is termed as "unsafe food" in terms of Section 3(zz)(viii) of FSSA Act and violation thereof is punishable u/s 59(1) of FSSA.

So if we go through both these provisions of law a particular offence with a particular fact is mentioned with some other Munish Kumar vs Delhi Administration/ on 18 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124526483/
5 name but with same ingredients in the New FSSA Act.

- Sub-clause (viii) of 3(zz) FSSA Act is applicable where the colouring material or the preservative other than that specified in respect there of is found in the food article and not where the colouring material exceeds the prescribed limit.
15.6 Further, the charge in this case was framed for the said offences and there is no charge in which it is stated that the said adulteration was injuries to health.

Had it been the case, the charge would have been for the offence punishable u/s 16(1-A)(ii) of PFA Act r/w section 2(ia)(l) & (f).
CA no. 8687/2016 Munish Kumar Ram Gopal Vs. Delhi Admn (PFA) Pages 10 of 14 15.7

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, it is held that it is the ingredients which constitute an offence and determines whether it is the same offence but with new name or an altogether different offence,

Here the offence of adding colour in the food article which was punishable u/s 16(1)(a) PFA Act is similar to the offence u/s 59 of FSSAI Act, which is now punishable with simple imprisonment of six months and fine upto one lakh.
15.8 Now, coming to the application of Nemi Chand Judgment (supra), the same is based on the old judgment i.e. T Barai ( Supra) of Hon'ble Supreme Court.

The relevant portion of the T Barai Judgment is as follows :
- (Para 25) It is settled both on authority and principle that when a later statute again describes an offence created by an earlier statute and imposes a different punishment or varies the procedure, the earlier statute is repealed by implication in Michell Vs.
Brown ( 1958) 120 ER 909, 912 : 32 LTOS 146:7 WR 80 Lord Campbell put the matter thus :
- "It is well settled rule of construction that, if a later statute again describes an ofence created by a former statute and affixes a different punishment, varying the procedure, the earlier statute is repealed by the later statute see also Smith Vs.
Benabo ( 1937) 1 ALL ER 523 : ( 1997) 1 KB 518: 156 LT 194"
- In Regina Vs. Youle ( 1861) 158 ER 311,315-16 : LT 299 : 9 WR 637 Martin B. said in the oft-quoted passage :
- If a statute deals with a particular class of offences, and a subsequent Act is passed which deals with precisely the same CA no. 8687/2016 Munish Kumar Ram Gopal Vs. Delhi Admn (PFA) Pages 11 of 14 offence, and a different punishment is imposed by the later Act, I think that, in effect, the legislature has declared that the new Act shall be substituted for the earlier Act."

- The rule is however subject to the limitation contained in Article 20(1) against ex post facto law providing for a greater punishment and has also no application where the offence described in the later Act is not the same as in the earlier Act i.e. when the essential ingredients of the two offences are different.

- To illustrate, if Parliament were to reenact Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code,
1860 and provide that the punishment for an offence of murder shall be sentence for imprisonment for life instead of the present sentence of death or imprisonment for life, then it can not be that the courts would still award a sentence of death even in pending cases.
15-A - Academic Reference can also be made to the letter dated 03.10.2017 of Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, produced before the court during the proceedings.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Vide said letter the said authority, in the light of judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Nemi Chand's Case (supra) issued an advisory to the Commissioners of Food Safety/Officers incharge of Food Safety to dispose of the long pending court cases filed under old PFA Act mainly concerning substandard and misbranding by imposing fine only.

15-B - In view of the above mentioned discussion, it can be safely CA no. 8687/2016 Munish Kumar Ram Gopal Vs. Delhi Admn (PFA) Pages 12 of 14 said that while considering the point of sentence,
in backdrop of the object and reasons of the act and the intention of the legislature, the quantum of sentence so passed in the interest of justice needs to be considered under the new Act i.e. FSSAI,
while deciding the present appeal.

sentences.text: 16. Thus, analyzing the facts of the case, taking note of the special circumstances of the case and the fact that accused has faced the trial of almost 16 years ; and in light of the above cited judgment and the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi titled as GNCT Vs. Jagdish Tyagi dated 11.10.2017 in my view the convict/ appellant is entitled to the benefit of new legislation.

Accordingly to meet the ends of justice, the sentence of the convict N0. 1 Munish Kumar and appellant no. 2 Ram Gopal,
imposed by the learned trial court vide order dated 11.05.2016 stands modified to the extent that the order sentencing the appellants to undergo simple imprisonment of one year stands waived of to simple imprisonment for one day i.e. till rising of the court ; the sentence of fine imposed upon appellant no. 1 enhanced from Rs. 20,000/- to Rs. 40,000/- and upon appellant no. 2 enhanced from Rs. 20,000/- to Rs. 60,000/-
In default of payment of fine the appellants/convicts shall undergo simple imprisonment for two months.
Sentence modified accordingly.

This was violation of Rules under PFA Rules and thus termed as adulteration in view of Section 2(1a)(a) (m) of the PFA Act and thus consequently punishable under section 16(1)(a)
of PFA Act read with Section 7 of PFA Act.
15.5
That now in the FSSAI such adulteration is termed as "unsafe food" in terms of Section 3(zz)(viii) of FSSA Act and violation thereof is punishable u/s 59(1) of FSSA.
Had it been the case, the charge would have been for the offence punishable u/s 16(1-A)(ii) of PFA Act r/w section 2(ia)(l) & (f).
CA no. 8687/2016 Munish Kumar Ram Gopal Vs. Delhi Admn (PFA) Pages 10 of 14 15.7
- The rule is however subject to the limitation contained in Article 20(1) against ex post facto law providing for a greater punishment and has also no application where the offence described in the later Act is not the same as in the earlier Act i.e. when the essential ingredients of the two offences are different.
Munish Kumar vs Delhi Administration/ on 18 January, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124526483/
6 - Moreover, this particular aspect is stated as a illustration in the same judgment in Para 23 which is as follows :
- To illustrate, if Parliament were to reenact Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code,
1860 and provide that the punishment for an offence of murder shall be sentence for imprisonment for life instead of the present sentence of death or imprisonment for life, then it can not be that the courts would still award a sentence of death even in pending cases.
15-A - Academic Reference can also be made to the letter dated 03.10.2017 of Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, produced before the court during the proceedings.
